_comment: Scheduled FRACTAL Runner — target registry. Adding a repo to the rotation is an edit HERE, not new code. PORTABLE: no absolute machine paths live in this file. Sibling-repo paths are built from config.repos_root (override per machine with the FRACTAL_REPOS_ROOT env var); this runner's own plugin paths are derived from the script location. So any operator's machine shares this file unchanged and only sets FRACTAL_REPOS_ROOT. Two scopes: registry targets get the FULL treatment (PR review + HANDOFF evidence); the --review-requested sweep adds review-only PRs. This registry ships with exactly one target, this repo (fractal-agent-system) itself, so the runner is structurally complete and testable out of the box. Operators add their own repos as additional entries.

config._repos_root_note: No default on purpose — committed config should never bake in an absolute machine path. Set FRACTAL_REPOS_ROOT to the directory containing your sibling repo checkouts before running, e.g. FRACTAL_REPOS_ROOT=$(cd .. && pwd) — repo_path = ${FRACTAL_REPOS_ROOT}/${target.repo_dir}.

config._tools_note: SECURITY: we review UNTRUSTED PR code, so treat the headless agent as prompt-injected. Per-command Bash allowlisting is POROUS — exec-capable 'read' tools (find -exec, rg --pre, sed e, awk system, xargs, gh api POST/DELETE) bypass a top-level deny list because the injected command runs as their CHILD. So: (1) permission-mode=default; (2) prefer Claude's NATIVE Read/Grep/Glob (no shell, no escape) for code inspection; (3) the Bash allowlist holds ONLY non-exec commands — review mode is read-only with no find/rg/sed/awk/gh-api; live adds gh pr comment/review (+ gh api, needed for inline comments — itself mutation-capable, hence gated); (4) a deny list explicitly blocks the exec vectors AND interpreters (perl/python/ruby/node/sh) as belt-and-suspenders. tests/test-allowlist-safety.sh statically guards that exec-capable tokens never re-enter the allowlists. RESIDUAL: this is hardening, not a sandbox — gh-read still reaches what the token can, and live's gh api can mutate. The robust fix is a --permission-prompt-tool classifier OR a no-egress sandbox (bwrap, worktree read-only, network limited to api.github.com). Until that lands: the untrusted SWEEP is DISABLED (sweep.enabled=false) and LIVE is registry-only after operator sign-off.

sweep._note: DISABLED pending the --permission-prompt-tool classifier / no-egress sandbox. The sweep is the genuinely untrusted path — arbitrary external repos the operator is review-requested on — where prompt-injection risk is highest. Re-enable only once the headless review runs inside a sandbox or behind a strict allow/deny classifier. Per-user by construction (@me = whoever's gh login); a swept PR whose repo has no registered local checkout is logged as SKIP, never cloned.

targets.gate_cmd: npm run lint && npm run build
